question: A depot audit ends with a single energy figure in kilojoules. A skip of mass 52 kg travels along the rail at a speed, in metres per second, worked out as 8 multiplied by the sum of 4 and 1. The energy the moving skip carries is the base amount. To that the auditor adds 30 J already stored in the buffer spring. A train holds 12 skips, so a train carries 12 times the corrected amount, and the depot dispatches 9 such trains. What is the depot figure, in kJ?

A quarry report closes with one number in kilonewtons. A skip whose mass plate reads 159000 g is accelerated up the incline. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the exact area under the curve y = 4x^2 + 0x between x = 2 and x = 3. The haul rope must supply the force that gives that skip that acceleration, and 3 N of that force is taken up by the guide roller and subtracted. The remainder is written in kilonewtons, after which two corrections are added in those same kilonewton units: 2 for the drum offset and 25 for the standing preload. The quarry pond holds 800 L of water, which is no part of this. What number closes the report, in kN?

A pinball workshop tests a ball whose mass plate reads 8000 g. Its launch speed, in metres per second, equals the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the machine's 11 bumpers, taken 2 at a time. The energy the moving ball carries is the raw reading, from which 3 J is subtracted for plunger friction. Each machine fires 11 balls in a test, so a machine total is 11 times the corrected reading, and the workshop runs 2 machines. The result is finally written in kilojoules. A 4 L tin of cabinet varnish sits on the shelf and has nothing to do with the test. What is the workshop total, in kJ?

A model-boat club adds together the whole numbers k for k running from 1 to 7. That sum is the launch speed, in metres per second, of a boat of mass 8 kg. The energy the moving boat carries is the raw reading. The club adds 7 J stored in the elastic and subtracts 3 J lost in the guide rail. Twelve boats are launched in the regatta, so the regatta energy is 12 times that corrected single-boat figure, and 25 J is then subtracted for the timing beam. A 60 L tank fills the test pool and is not relevant. What is the regatta figure, in J?

A dairy loads two batches of 258 and 266 identical churns into equal full pallets, choosing the largest pallet size that divides both counts exactly. A cart whose mass plate reads 40000 g is then rolled at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that pallet size. The energy the moving cart carries is the base value, and with 5 carts on the floor the floor energy is 5 times it. The log writes that total in kilojoules. It then subtracts 6 and then 4, both in those same kilojoule units, for the two meter corrections. What does the log record, in kJ?

A shipyard winch accelerates a block whose mass plate reads 184000 g. The acceleration given to the block, in metres per second squared, is the exact area under the curve y = 2x^2 + 3x between x = 0 and x = 1. The winch must supply the force that gives that block that acceleration. Seven blocks are hauled together, so the gang force is 7 times one block's figure, and the log writes that in kilonewtons. Nine gangs work a berth, and the yard has 2 berths. A 500 L ballast tank stands nearby and plays no part. What is the yard total, in kN?

A mine hoist report ends with one number in newtons. A cage whose mass plate reads 199000 g is accelerated up the shaft. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the exact area under the curve y = 5x^2 + 6x between x = 0 and x = 3. The rope must supply the force that gives that cage that acceleration, and 3 N of it is absorbed by the shaft guide and subtracted. Five cages share a shaft, so the shaft demand is 5 times the corrected figure. The mine has 9 shafts, and the group operates 12 identical mines. What is the group total, in N?

An engine test cell drives a mass of 116 kg along a rail. The control curve is y = 3x^3 + 4x^2, and the engineer first finds how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at x = 2. Adding 3 to that value gives the acceleration, in metres per second squared, applied to the mass. The rail must supply the force that produces that acceleration. Six rails run in a cell and 7 cells run in the building, so the building demand is 6 times the single-rail force and then 7 times that. The cell's air line is charged to 9 bar, which is irrelevant here. What is the building demand, in kN?

A gymnastics rig report ends with one number in kilojoules. A trolley whose mass plate reads 12000 g runs along a beam at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 3x^2 + 5x between x = 1 and x = 2. The energy the moving trolley carries is the base value, and the report writes that in kilojoules. From the recorded value 26 is subtracted, in those same kilojoule units, as the rig's standing allowance. The hall contains 9 identical rigs, so the hall figure is 9 times the corrected value. What number ends the report, in kJ?

A bobsleigh centre's summary ends with one figure in kilojoules. A sled whose mass plate reads 49000 g leaves the ramp at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the slope of the curve y = 2x^3 - 2x^2 at x = 3. The energy the sled carries at that speed is the base value, which the summary records in kilojoules. Ten sleds run in a session, so the session energy is 10 times the record, and 21 is then added in those same kilojoule units for the start-house machinery. The centre holds 11 identical sessions. What figure ends the summary, in kJ?

A go-kart circuit tests a kart whose mass plate reads 14000 g. Its speed along the straight, in metres per second, is the larger root of x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0. The energy the moving kart carries is the base value. Five karts run in a heat, so a heat's energy is 5 times that base value, and the timing system records the heat total in kilojoules. A meeting comprises 12 heats, so the meeting energy is 12 times the recorded heat figure, and 19 is then added in those same kilojoule units for the paddock equipment. What is the meeting figure, in kJ?

A laboratory glider whose mass plate reads 47000 g slides along an air track. Its speed, in metres per second, is the smaller root of x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0. The energy the moving glider carries is the raw reading, from which 7 J is subtracted for the launch-catch loss. The display converts what remains to kilojoules, then adds 10 and subtracts 23, both in those same kilojoule units, as the two standing instrument corrections. The bench also holds a 3 L water bath that plays no part. What does the display finally show, in kJ?

A ferry ramp test uses a trolley whose mass plate reads 44000 g. Its speed down the ramp, in metres per second, is 5 multiplied by the sum of 4 and 8. The energy the moving trolley carries is the base value. The rig then adds 10 J stored in the release spring and a further 6 J stored in the buffer. Ten trolleys are run in the trial, so the trial energy is 10 times that corrected single-trolley figure. The ramp itself is 25 m long, which is not needed. What is the trial energy, in J?

A launcher rig traces the curve y = 3x^2 + 2x and takes the exact area under it between x = 0 and x = 3. Adding 3 to that area gives the muzzle speed, in metres per second, of a projectile of mass 44 kg. The energy the projectile carries at that speed is the base reading. The rig then adds 21 J for the propellant residue and 26 J for the barrel spring, and finally subtracts 26 J absorbed by the recoil damper. The rig frame stands 6 m tall, which does not enter the calculation. What energy, in J, does the rig report?

A press line report closes with one number in newtons. A ram whose mass plate reads 106000 g is driven along its stroke. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the slope of the curve y = 4x^3 + 3x^2 at x = 2. The drive must supply the force that gives that ram that acceleration. Eight rams work a press, so the press force is 8 times one ram's figure, from which 21 N is subtracted for guide friction and a further 26 N for the return spring. The plant runs 12 identical presses. What number closes the report, in N?

A crane test sheet ends with one number in kilonewtons. A ballast block of mass 148 kg is driven along a rail. The control curve is y = 5x^3 + 2x^2, and the acceleration applied to the block, in metres per second squared, is how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at x = 2. The drive must supply the force that gives that block that acceleration, and 25 N of it is lost in the guide rollers and subtracted. The sheet writes the remainder in kilonewtons, then adds 1 in those same kilonewton units as the standing offset. The rig's hydraulic pack holds 40 L of oil, which plays no part. What number ends the sheet, in kN?

A cable-car works tests a carrier whose mass plate reads 193000 g. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger root of x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0. The haul rope must supply the force that gives that carrier that acceleration, and the log writes that force in kilonewtons. Twelve carriers run on the line, so the line demand is 12 times the logged value, and 11 is then added in those same kilonewton units for the drive-station tare. The station also has a 300 L water tank, which is not part of this. What is the final figure, in kN?

A curling club report ends with a single number in kilojoules. A stone whose mass plate reads 13000 g slides down the sheet at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the larger root of x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0. The energy the moving stone carries is the raw reading. From it 23 J is subtracted for the ice friction and a further 26 J for the sweeping loss. The remainder is then written in kilojoules. The rink is held at 5 degrees Celsius, a figure that is not used. What number ends the report, in kJ?

A bookbindery groups two orders of 53 and 292 identical signatures into equal full bundles, using the largest bundle size that divides both counts exactly. A carriage whose mass plate reads 136000 g is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that bundle size. The belt must supply the force that gives that carriage that acceleration. Three carriages run per machine, so the machine force is 3 times one carriage's figure, and 29 N of clamp preload is added to it. The bindery has 7 machines, and the group runs 4 identical binderies. What is the group total, in N?

A skateboard test ramp is cut to the profile curve y = 4x^3 - 3x^2. A board of mass 5 kg leaves the lip at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the slope of that curve at x = 2. The energy the moving board carries is the base value, which the rig writes in kilojoules. From that record 18 is subtracted for the ramp allowance and a further 5 for the sensor offset, both in those same kilojoule units. Twelve runs make a session, so the session figure is 12 times the corrected value. The ramp's plywood deck is 18 mm thick, which is irrelevant here. What is the session figure, in kJ?

A ferry terminal log ends with one number in joules. A loading trolley of mass 55 kg rolls down the linkspan. Its speed, in metres per second, is found by taking 4 multiplied by the sum of 8 and 14, then subtracting 26 from that product. The energy the moving trolley carries is the raw reading, from which 26 J is subtracted for the buffer loss. Four trolleys are run for each sailing. What number ends the log, in J?

A ski-jump centre's sheet ends with one figure in kilojoules. A test sled whose mass plate reads 26000 g leaves the in-run at a speed, in metres per second, equal to how fast the slope of the curve y = 2x^3 + 3x^2 is itself changing at x = 3. The energy the moving sled carries is the base value, recorded in kilojoules. Eight runs make a session, so the session energy is 8 times that record. From the session total 27 is subtracted and then 1 is added, both in those same kilojoule units, for the two standing corrections. What figure ends the sheet, in kJ?

A mining conveyor report ends with one figure in kilojoules. The control curve is y = 4x^2 + 5x, and the exact area under it between x = 2 and x = 4 is taken first; subtracting 28 from that area gives the speed, in metres per second, of the skip. The skip's mass plate reads 40000 g, and the energy it carries at that speed is the base value, recorded in kilojoules. Five skips run per drift, so the drift energy is 5 times the record. A further 28 is then added in those same kilojoule units for the tipping gear. What figure ends the report, in kJ?

A physics demonstration ends with one number in kilojoules. The demonstrator writes out k^2 for k running from 1 to 4, adds the four values together, and then subtracts 1 from that sum. The result is the speed, in metres per second, of a trolley whose mass plate reads 10000 g. The energy the moving trolley carries is the base value, which the display shows in kilojoules. From that displayed value 29 is subtracted, in those same kilojoule units, as the standing offset. What is the number at the end, in kJ?

A packaging machine drives a carriage whose mass plate reads 21000 g. The control curve is y = 4x^3 + 2x^2, and the slope of that curve at x = 2 is found first; adding 21 to it gives the acceleration, in metres per second squared, applied to the carriage. The belt must supply the force that produces that acceleration, and 16 N of that force is absorbed by the tensioner and subtracted. Three carriages run on the machine, so the machine demand is 3 times the corrected single-carriage force. The log records the result in kilonewtons. What does the log record, in kN?
